## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vacībhedakathā* (Kv 2.5) is the fifth discourse of the second chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Skorupski 1991]. The debate investigates the thesis that there can be vocal utterance or verbal articulation (*vacībheda*) on the part of a practitioner who is in a meditative attainment (*samāpanna*) [Skorupski 1991; Bareau 1955]. This dispute addresses the fifth thesis in the controversy over Mahādeva's five points, which asserted that entry into the noble path (*mārga*) by one in meditative absorption can be accompanied by an exclamation—specifically uttering the word "suffering" (*dukkha*) upon realizing suffering [Skorupski 1991; Lamotte 1988]. In the *Kathāvatthu*, the Theravādin refutation questions whether knowing suffering necessitates vocalizing the word [Skorupski 1991]. Sectarian doxographies by Bhavya and others ascribe this proposition to the Mahāsāṃghika and Ekavyavahārika traditions [Skorupski 1991; Bareau 1955].
SuttaCentral notes that the debate relates to discourses discussing the gradual cessation of vocal activity and speech in meditation, such as the *Rahogatasutta* (SN 36.11) and related suttas of the *Vedanā Saṃyutta* (SN 36.15–18; SA 473, SA 474), the *Kaṇṭakasutta* (AN 10.72), the *Anupubbanirodhasutta* (AN 9.31), and the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records 1,714 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 93 texts; the longest alignments are with the *Vedanā Saṃyutta* (SN 36.11), the *Navakanipāta* (AN 9.31), and the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), directly agreeing with the textual parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Other Kathāvatthu debates showing heavy text reuse include Kv 3.6, Kv 1.6, Kv 18.8, Kv 8.10, Kv 8.2, and Kv 12.9, alongside citations in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments automatically with cross-language parallels including the Sanskrit *Mahāvyutpatti* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
